findings.finding: A skip that completes the run emits no event carrying the run status: the in-loop path emits only recovery and phase_skipped (neither has a run status), the generic recover-phase-task path nothing about completion; events.jsonl consumers never see this run finish.
findings.suggestion: Add runStatus=recovered.get('run_status') to the recovery emit, or emit a completion signal from mark_loop_complete, or document that events are not a completion source.

findings.finding: The new run_status==complete branch sits under the comment saying skipped/failed recoveries leave the pointer, and recover_single_session's docstring does not mention the completion stamp.
findings.suggestion: Move the mark_loop_complete call above that comment with its own comment and add a docstring sentence.

findings.finding: The early-return branch duplicates the closing _write_config + _ok of the main path (two exits, correct).
findings.suggestion: Optional: collect run_status into an extra dict and keep one exit.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: the config write and the loop-state write cannot leave an inconsistent pair — The loop stamp runs after the locked config write, outside the lock; if save_loop_state fails or the process dies between them, run_config says complete and the loop says stopped, and a retried skip cannot heal it because _completion_unblocked returns False on a complete run so mark_loop_complete is never reached.
findings.suggestion: Make mark_loop_complete self-healing: call it whenever the run's status is complete, not only on the transition.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: --force-status failed never completes a run — recover X failed (run stays needs_validation), then recover Y skipped: TERMINAL_STATUSES counts failed as terminal so the run completes with X failed. complete_phase_task applies the same rule, but the stated claim is only true one call at a time.
findings.suggestion: Require no failed task, or rebut as matching complete_phase_task and reword the claim; add a failed-then-skip test either way.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: absence of validation_issues reliably means the lifecycle produced the pause — A malformed v1 pause with validation_issues [] would be popped by update_step while status stays needs_validation, indistinguishable from the lifecycle pause.
findings.suggestion: A positive lifecycle marker, or rebut that v1 configs never reach this state.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: mark_loop_complete on the generic CLI is safe for non-single-session configs — The router path has no mode check; only loop_state presence and runId match guard it.
findings.suggestion: Add an is_single_session(config) check or document why runId suffices.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: completing on all-terminal never closes a run with unmaterialised work — Skipping an open plan/split-N does not plan its build successor, so the run completes with split N never built.
findings.suggestion: Accept as operator intent and document, or check for unmaterialised successors.
